issues.description: The problem text for Aufgabe 06 refers to a column named 'Weibliche_Personen' (line 133), but the solution and the rest of the exercises consistently use the column name 'einwohner_w' (solution_repository/aufgabe06.sql). This name mismatch can confuse students about which column to use when writing their WHERE clause and may lead them to search for a non-existent column name in the schema or template.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the column name consistent across artifacts. Either change the problem statement to refer to 'einwohner_w' (e.g. "... mehr als 100.000 einwohner_w ...") or update the solution and any schema references to use 'Weibliche_Personen'. The simplest fix is to update the problem statement text for Aufgabe 06 to use 'einwohner_w' so it matches the schema and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement for Aufgabe 06 explicitly refers to a column named 'Weibliche_Personen' as the female population column, but the solution implementation (and other tasks) use the column name einwohner_w. This naming mismatch (Weibliche_Personen vs. einwohner_w) refers to the same conceptual entity (female inhabitants) but uses different identifiers across artifacts. Students following the problem text may write queries using 'Weibliche_Personen' and get errors or fail to map the requirement to the provided schema/solution, creating unnecessary cognitive load.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the identifier for the female population column across all artifacts. Either change the problem text to refer to the existing column einwohner_w (e.g.: "...und mehr als 100.000 einwohner_w (Spaltenname) ...") or alter the solution/template to use the column name Weibliche_Personen. Preferably update the problem statement to 'einwohner_w' to match the schema and solution, and add a short note listing the exact column names (einwohner_m, einwohner_w) to avoid future confusion.
